ai.title: CONTRIBUTING.md: GitHub OAuth setup, simplified credits
ai.summary: CONTRIBUTING.md adds GitHub OAuth app setup (CODEBUFF_GITHUB_ID/SECRET via Infisical) as step 7. Credits instructions simplified: replace manual Stripe/DB row creation with login at localhost:3000/login then edit existing credit_ledger principal/balance. Renumbered steps 8-10. Internal docs only.

eli5.text: If you want to sign into the assistant using your GitHub account while helping build it, the setup guide now walks you through creating a GitHub login app and storing its keys in the project's secret vault. The old, more technical instructions for boosting your own test balance, like typing fake credit-card numbers and manually editing database rows, are replaced with a simpler path: log in at the local website, then just change one number in the dashboard. The rest of the steps got shifted down by one to make room, but nothing else about the developer workflow changed.

ai.title: Test-mode exception for message and usage persistence
ai.summary: Added NODE_ENV === 'test' guards to insertMessageRecordWithRetries and updateUserCycleUsageWithRetries in backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts. These bypass throw-on-failure behavior for test environments, returning null or { consumed: 0, fromPurchased: 0 } instead. The return type of insertMessageRecordWithRetries widened to Promise<typeof schema.message.$inferSelect | null>. Scope limited to backend message-cost-tracker.ts; no user-facing surfaces affected.

eli5.text: When the system runs in its behind-the-scenes testing mode, saving a message or updating a user's usage counters no longer crashes the whole test run if the database write fails. Instead, the system quietly logs the problem and pretends nothing went wrong, returning an empty result so tests can keep moving. This only affects the internal testing environment and has no impact on real usage.

ai.title: Rename test environment check to NEXTPUBLICCBENVIRONMENT
ai.summary: The `message-cost-tracker.ts` file now checks `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT === 'test'` instead of `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'test'`. This aligns the backend cost-tracking retry logic with the unified frontend environment variable standard. No functional changes outside of this variable name update.

eli5.text: When the cost-tracking system fails to save a message after several retries, it now checks a different environment label to decide whether to quietly return zero costs instead of raising an error. This new label, NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT, replaces the old NODE_ENV check, so the system now matches the same environment-setting convention used across the frontend and backend. If you were not already using this new label in test mode, you would notice the quiet fallback no longer triggering as expected.

eli5.text: The team quietly turned off one of their automated tests for a part of the app that handles work items and project details. This test was meant to check that things like descriptions, estimates, and assignments are filled in correctly, but it was too confusing to be useful, so they pulled it out instead of trying to fix it. You won't see any difference in your day-to-day work - the app features they were testing are still there and still work the same way. It's just like removing a checklist question that didn't make sense during a training exercise; the training itself continues, just with slightly fewer steps.

ai.title: Add cb bin alias to npm-app release package
ai.summary: Added 'cb' as a bin alias pointing to index.js in the npm-app/release/package.json. This provides a shorter command-line invocation alongside the existing 'codebuff' entry. The change applies only to the published npm package structure.

eli5.text: The assistant can now be started from the command line using the shorter word 'cb' in addition to the existing full command. This only affects how developers invoke the tool in their terminal; typing 'cb' instead of the longer name runs the same program. The shorter alias is available today in the installed package.

ai.title: Deprecate agentId in AgentStateSchema
ai.summary: Marked agentId as deprecated in common/src/types/session-state.ts, indicating replacement by runId. backend/src/run-agent-step.ts updated to log runId, totalSteps, directCreditsUsed, and agentType alongside agentId on execution failure.

eli5.text: The system now records a new identifier alongside the old one when a step in an agent run fails. If a step fails, the error log you'd inspect will include the agent type, the agent's unique run identifier, the total number of steps attempted, and the direct credits used by that agent, in addition to the old agent identifier that is being phased out. For now, the old identifier still exists in the data definition and the new identifier is simply added to the failure logs; the old identifier hasn't been removed yet.

ai.title: message-cost-tracker returns null on retry exhaustion
ai.summary: Removed throw error in `insertMessageRecordWithRetries` and `updateUserCycleUsageWithRetries`. Now returns `null` or `{ consumed: 0, fromPurchased: 0 }` after max retries fail. Eliminates special-case handling for `NEXT_PUBLIC_CB_ENVIRONMENT === 'test'`. Internal change in `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts`.

eli5.text: When the system tried to record a message bill and ran out of retries, it now quietly gives up and returns a no-charge placeholder instead of throwing an error. This affects the billing and usage-tracking flow that runs behind the scenes for all internal environments (including test), so test-mode users no longer hit a special exception, everyone gets the same fail-safe path. If you watched the logs, the loud "couldn't fetch usage" error for test mode is gone, replaced by a silent return of zero usage, and the code now keeps the old throw commented out as a future consideration rather than removed entirely.

ai.title: Run git add before diffing files in git evals
ai.summary: The `getCodebuffFileStates` function in `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts` now executes `git add .` before running `git diff`. This ensures uncommitted changes are staged and captured in the diff output. The scope is limited to the internal git evaluation suite.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the internal evaluation tool that checks how the assistant handles file changes now runs a "prepare" step before taking its snapshot. This only affects the internal testing suite, not anything you experience directly. If you were looking at the system that scores those tests, you'd see it staging any in-progress work before capturing the diff, so the evaluation measures the full set of changes instead of only saved ones.

ai.title: User input cancellation no longer throws error
ai.summary: Agent loop in backend/src/run-agent-step.ts now breaks instead of throwing Error('User input no longer live (likely cancelled)') when checkLiveUserInput fails. Log severity upgraded from debug to warn. Prevents unhandled exceptions during cancellation.

eli5.text: When you cancel what you're doing mid-way, the system stops quietly instead of popping an error message at you. This only affects the background assistant process while it's working through your request, and you wouldn't see anything unusual unless you were already watching the system logs, where the quieter debug note about the cancellation is now louder and labeled as a warning.

ai.title: Add CONTEXT7APIKEY to env schema and auth headers
ai.summary: Added optional `CONTEXT7_API_KEY` to `packages/internal/src/env.ts` schema and injected it into `Authorization` headers for `searchLibraries` and `fetchContext7LibraryDocumentation` in `backend/src/llm-apis/context7-api.ts`. This enables authenticated access to Context7 API endpoints. Also reduced default `max_tokens` for `read-docs` tool from 20,000 to 10,000 in `common/src/tools/params/tool/read-docs.ts`.

eli5.text: The assistant can now access a documentation service called Context7 when looking up library information, if a secret key for that service is configured. When you ask it to read documentation, it will now return a smaller default amount of text from each source. You would not notice anything yet unless the proper setup key is provided, and then library lookups would work with an authenticated connection.
